description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted

observations.note: They said they cook every Sunday, whatever else is going on, and described it as a weekly reset; chopping vegetables clears their head.
observations.hook: A dependable weekly ritual that helps create a sense of reset through hands-on, repetitive preparation.
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: They made shakshuka with cumin and a bit of feta that morning.
They usually choose what to cook on Sunday morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Making a choice in the moment using whatever ingredients are available.
observations.quote: Usually decide that morning based on whatever's in the fridge.

observations.note: They made ramen from scratch, spending seven hours on the broth; they said the tare was the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: They had been studying Japanese with Duolingo for about three months and could read some of the soy sauce bottle label; they said nobody had asked them to learn it and they wanted to.
observations.hook: Choosing to learn a language from personal interest, and noticing it become useful in an everyday moment
observations.caveat: They could read only some of the label.
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: They felt kind of proud that their Japanese practice let them read some of the soy sauce label.
observations.hook: A practiced skill becoming useful in an ordinary real-world moment
observations.caveat: They could read only some of the label.

observations.note: They asked how sakoku affected what people ate in Edo and whether sushi came from that era, noting this was beyond the syllabus.
observations.hook: Understanding culture through the history of food, beyond what a class requires

observations.note: They said they chose the elective to understand the culture behind food and the language they are into.
observations.topic: Reason for choosing Japanese history elective
observations.hook: Connecting food and language with the culture behind them
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: They called sushi being fast food funny, reacting to the contrast between a familiar food and its historical role as quick street food.
observations.hook: The surprising contrast between a familiar food and its past role as fast food
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: They said they wanted to visit Kyoto someday and were saving up for it, perhaps for next year.
observations.hook: The temple scenes in anime drew them to the idea of visiting Kyoto.
observations.quote: I really want to go to Kyoto someday, the temple scenes in anime always get me.
